# `starhermit:nav`

Engine **1.42.0** (host API 1.42), the latest release. Generated from the release's `starhermit.d.ts`; `starhermit types` writes the same file into your game. [All modules](index.md).

```ts
import { … } from "starhermit:nav";
```

Navigation for game agents (since API\_MINOR 42, `NAV_MINOR`; for a game declaring an older `engine.minor` the import throws a TypeError as the module evaluates). An engine extension: three.js has no navigation. Run natively (starhermit-nav), so a mesh, a path and a crowd come to the same bits natively and in browsers. Y is up.

A NavMesh is built from triangles: they are voxelised (cellSize across, cellHeight up), the floors an agent of agentHeight can stand on (no steeper than agentMaxSlope, steps of at most agentMaxClimb to their neighbours) are kept, those nearer an edge (a wall, a drop) than agentRadius are dropped, and the rest are covered by planar convex polygons. Bake one with toBytes and ship it; NavMesh.fromBytes reads it back (checked). Queries: A\* over the polygons with string pulling, area costs and areas left out (NavQueryFilter), off-mesh links (jumps, drops, ladders), the nearest point, a ray cast along the mesh, random points. NavGrid is A\* over a 2D grid for tile games; Crowd steers agents along paths (arrival, separation, collision, links).

Bounds: a build takes at most 1,048,576 triangles and a voxel grid of 4,194,304 columns; at most 16 meshes (1,048,576 polygons in all), 16 grids (8,388,608 cells in all, 4096 a side), 8 crowds (256 agents each) and 64 filters at once (a RangeError past them; dispose() lets one go). A path opens at most maxNodes polygons (4096 by default, at most 65,536); a crowd plans at most 8 paths an update.

Fuel: a build about 20 instructions a triangle, 10 a voxel interval and 100 a polygon (a 20 m room at 0.3 m cells about 60,000); a path about 30 a polygon opened; a crowd's update about 150 an agent plus its searches.

### NavMeshBuildOptions

*interface*

```ts
export interface NavMeshBuildOptions { … }
```

- `cellSize?: number;`

  Voxel width and depth (default 0.3) and height (0.2), world units.

- `cellHeight?: number;`

- `agentHeight?: number;`

  The agent: height (2), radius (0.6), highest step (0.9), steepest slope in degrees (45).

- `agentRadius?: number;`
- `agentMaxClimb?: number;`
- `agentMaxSlope?: number;`

- `regionMinSize?: number;`

  Islands of fewer than this many cells squared are dropped (8).

- `maxPolySize?: number;`

  The most cells a polygon spans in x or z (64; 1 to 256).

- `heightError?: number;`

  How far a floor may be from its polygon's plane (0.4).

- `bounds?: { min: Vec3Like; max: Vec3Like };`

  The region built (default: the triangles' bounds).

- `areaBoxes?: { min: Vec3Like; max: Vec3Like; area: number }[];`

  Boxes whose walkable floors take an area id (1 to 63; 0 cuts them out).

- `areas?: ArrayLike<number>;`

  An area id a triangle (0 unwalkable; default 63, NAV\_WALKABLE\_AREA).

### NavMesh

*class*

```ts
export class NavMesh { … }
```

- `private constructor();`

- `static fromTriangles(positions: ArrayLike<number>, indices?: ArrayLike<number> | null, options?: NavMeshBuildOptions): NavMesh;`

  Builds from triangles: three numbers a vertex, three indices a triangle (or none: the vertices in threes). Triangles facing up (counter-clockwise seen from above, three.js's front faces) are walkable. A TypeError for bad input, a RangeError when too big.

- `static fromObject(object: import("starhermit:scene").Object3D, options?: NavMeshBuildOptions & { filter?: (mesh: import("starhermit:scene").Mesh) => boolean }): NavMesh;`

  Builds from the Meshes and InstancedMeshes under `object` (and it), in world space; `filter` chooses which meshes count.

- `static fromBytes(bytes: ArrayBuffer | ArrayBufferView): NavMesh;`

  A mesh baked by `toBytes` (a TypeError when the bytes are not one).

- `toBytes(): Uint8Array;`

  The mesh and its off-mesh links as bytes.

- `readonly buildStats: NavMeshBuildStats | null;`

  What the build came to (null for a mesh read from bytes).

- `readonly polygonCount: number;`
- `readonly vertexCount: number;`
- `readonly offMeshLinkCount: number;`
- `readonly bounds: { min: NavPoint; max: NavPoint };`
- `readonly agent: { cellSize: number; radius: number; height: number; maxClimb: number };`

- `addOffMeshLink(start: Vec3Like, end: Vec3Like, options?: { radius?: number; bidirectional?: boolean; area?: number; userId?: number }): { index: number; joined: boolean };`

  An off-mesh link from `start` to `end`, each end joining the mesh within `radius` (1); both ways unless `bidirectional` is false; its cost is its length times its area's (63 by default). `joined` is false when an end found no polygon: the link is never taken.

- `findPath(start: Vec3Like, end: Vec3Like, options?: NavQueryOptions): NavPath | null;`

  The cheapest path's corners from `start` to `end`; null when an end is off the mesh.

- `findNearestPoint(point: Vec3Like, options?: NavQueryOptions): NavPoint | null;`

- `raycast(start: Vec3Like, end: Vec3Like, options?: { filter?: NavQueryFilter }): NavRaycastHit | null;`

  A ray along the mesh from `start` (snapped to it) towards `end`.

- `randomPoint(random?: () => number, options?: { filter?: NavQueryFilter }): NavPoint | null;`

  A point on the mesh, uniform by area, from three draws of `random` (Math.random by default; pass a seeded one to repeat).

- `debugGeometry(): { edges: Float32Array; walls: Float32Array; links: Float32Array; triangles: Float32Array; areas: Uint8Array };`

  For a debug view: edges between polygons, walls and links (six floats a segment), the polygons as triangles (nine floats each) and each triangle's area.

- `dispose(): void;`

### createNavMeshHelper

*function*

```ts
export function createNavMeshHelper(navMesh: NavMesh, SCENE: typeof import("starhermit:scene"), options?: { lift?: number; fillOpacity?: number }): import("starhermit:scene").Group;
```

A debug view of a mesh as a Group of the scene module passed (`import * as SCENE from "starhermit:scene"`; starhermit:nav does not import it, so a 2D game using only NavGrid gets no 3D scene): the polygons coloured by area, `fillOpacity` (0.35) see-through, their edges, the walls and the links, `lift` (0.05) above the mesh.

### NavGridPathOptions

*interface*

```ts
export interface NavGridPathOptions { … }
```

- `diagonal?: boolean;`

  Eight ways (true, the default; never cutting a blocked corner) or four.

- `smooth?: boolean;`

  Drop corners a straight line of open cells joins (false). A path whose smoothing walks over 67,108,864 cells of line-of-sight checks in all is refused (a RangeError): smooth shorter paths.

- `maxNodes?: number;`

  The most cells opened (65,536; at most 1,048,576).

### NavGrid

*class*

A 2D grid for tile games: each cell a cost, 0 blocked, 1 to 255 what a step into it costs (√2 times that diagonally). All 1 at first.

### Crowd

*class*

Agents walking a NavMesh: each steers for its path's next corner, slows to a stop at its target, keeps apart from others (to the right of one coming at it), is pushed out of others it overlaps, slides along walls and is carried along off-mesh links at its top speed.

```ts
export class Crowd { … }
```

- `constructor(navMesh: NavMesh, options?: { filter?: NavQueryFilter });`

- `addAgent(position: Vec3Like, params?: CrowdAgentParams): number;`

  An agent at the mesh's point nearest `position`; its id, or -1.

- `removeAgent(id: number): void;`

- `setTarget(id: number, target: Vec3Like | null): void;`

  Sends it to `target` (null stops it).

- `update(seconds: number): void;`

  Moves every agent on (from onFixedUpdate, say; at most a second).

- `getAgent(id: number): CrowdAgent | null;`
- `readonly agentIds: number[];`
- `dispose(): void;`
